BURSEVI:v4p174/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r5.claim: Yughāth may mean rain is sent, from the three-letter root ghayth, or people are rescued, from the four-letter root ghawth; the alif reflects the respective root vowel.
BURSEVI:v4p174/r5.anchor: أي يمطرون فيكون بناؤه من ثلاثي

BURSEVI:v4p174/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r6.claim: Alternatively, the form may derive from ghawth and mean rescue from hardship.

BURSEVI:v4p174/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r7.claim: In the prosperous year, abundance lets people press grapes, sugarcane, olives, sesame, and similar produce.
BURSEVI:v4p174/r7.anchor: ما شأنه أن يعصر من العنب والقصب والزيتون والسمسم

BURSEVI:v4p174/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r8.claim: The repeated ‘in it’ distinguishes rain and relief, acts of God, from pressing, an act people perform.
BURSEVI:v4p174/r8.anchor: وتكرير فيه لأن الغيث والغوث من فعل الله والعصر من فعل الناس

BURSEVI:v4p174/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p174/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p174/r9.claim: The final year’s glad tidings came by revelation, not from the king’s dream; the cows and ears symbolize fertile years, thin cows and dry ears famine, and stored abundance is consumed.
BURSEVI:v4p174/r9.anchor: وإنما تلقاه من جهة الوحي فبشرهم بها

QASHANI:12:49-51/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:49-51/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:49-51/r1.claim: The fruitful year of relief and pressing signifies the soul's enjoyment after complete tranquility and security.
QASHANI:12:49-51/r1.anchor: هو وقت تمتيعه للنفس عند الاطمئنان التام والأمن الكلي

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r1.claim: They read يعصرون in the third person, with the people previously mentioned as its subject.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر: يعصرون بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r2.claim: They read تعصرون in the second person, addressing the petitioners who asked Joseph for an interpretation.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r3.claim: The verb can mean pressing oil or juice in the coming fertile year; some interpreters say the people had gone fourteen years without pressing oil or grapes, while another sense is escaping to safety.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r3.anchor: وهذا يمكن أن يكون تأويل الآية عليه ، لأن من المتأولين

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p425#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses تعصرون as نجاة (being saved); poetry and related usages support العصر as a refuge or means of escape.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r2.speaker: عيسى والأعرج وجعفر بن محمد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r2.claim: These readers pronounce يُعْصَرون with a yāʾ and open ṣād; it can mean receiving rain or rescue, while Ibn ʿAbbās explains the rescue through pressing grapes or oils.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عيسى والأعرج وجعفر بن محمد: "وفيه يعصرون"8

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says يعصرون means they press grapes or oils; the poem's عصرة means relief or rescue for someone in distress.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p344/r3.anchor: وروينا عن ابن عباس: أي يعصرون من الكرم والأدهان

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p196/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p196/r1.claim: The yāʾ form of يعصرون refers back to الناس in the preceding clause; the tāʾ form singles the addressees out from other people.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p196/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأ بالياء أنه رده على قوله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r2.claim: These readers use yāʾ in يعصرون; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use tāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p349/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر

QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#1/r1.claim: The standard reading is active Form IV, third-person masculine plural.
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#1/r1.anchor: 3rd person masculine plural active IV — standard recitation

QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#2/r1.claim: The second-person plural reading changes the clause to direct address to Joseph's interlocutors.
QIRAAT-ER:12:49:12#2/r1.anchor: 2nd person plural active IV; direct address shifts to Joseph's interlocutors

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#3/r3.claim: God gave Joseph knowledge of an unasked eighth year, when rain comes and people press grapes and fruits.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p324#3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة فزاده الله علم سنة لم يسألوه عنها فقال ﴿ ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون ﴾ قال يعصرون الأعناب والثمار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.claim: Joseph's reply combines three kinds of speech: interpretation by meaning rather than wording, practical advice, and a report of the unseen future eighth year.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r1.anchor: والثالث: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the prediction of the eighth year as foreknowledge of the unseen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r2.anchor: والثالث: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows that this need not be unseen knowledge: the dream's interpretation itself implied hardship would end after seven years, followed by abundance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p285/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل هذا أن لا يكون غيبا، بل علم العبارة أعطى انقطاع الخوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and most exegetes derive yughāth from rain; another view derives it from relief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور: يغاث من الغيث، وقيل: من الغوث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r4.claim: The rain derivation is triliteral, while the relief derivation is quadriliteral.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r4.anchor: ففي الأول بني من ثلاثي، وفي الثاني من رباعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r5.speaker: الأخوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r5.claim: The two readers use second-person taʿṣirūn; the other seven use third-person yaʿṣirūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان: تعصرون بالتاء على الخطاب، وباقي السبعة بالياء على الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r6.claim: Most read the verb as squeezing plants and produce, including grapes, cane, olives, sesame, radish, and milk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أنه من عصر النبات كالعنب والقصب والزيتون والسمسم والفجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r7.claim: A report says people pressed nothing during the drought years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r7.anchor: وروي أنهم لم يعصروا شيئا مدة الجدب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda and others derive the word from ʿaṣra, deliverance, and cite Abu Zubayd’s verse about Uthman as refuge for the distressed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r8.anchor: والعصر وهو المنجي، ومنه قول أبي زبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r9.speaker: جعفر بن محمد، والأعرج، وعيسى البصرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r9.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, al-Aʿraj, and ʿIsa of Basra read a passive form, meaning people are delivered from hardship, matching yughāth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r9.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد، والأعرج، وعيسى البصرة يعصرون بضم الياء وفتح الصاد مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r10.speaker: عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r10.claim: A second reading from ʿIsa uses second-person passive taʿṣarūn, likewise meaning you are rescued from hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r10.anchor: وعن عيسى أيضا: تعصرون بالتاء على الخطاب مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r11.speaker: ابن المستنير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r11.claim: Ibn al-Mustanir reads it as rain falling on people, from a cloud releasing its water, with the action figuratively attributed to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r11.anchor: وقال ابن المستنير: معناه يمطرون، من أعصرت السحابة ماءها عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r12.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r12.claim: Al-Naqqash reports a doubled, intensive reading of yaʿṣirūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r12.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه قرىء يعصرون بضم الياء وكسر الصاد وشدها، من عصر مشددا للتكثير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r13.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads taʿtaṣirūn, formed by assimilating tāʾ into ṣād; it may mean squeezing or being delivered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r13.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: وفيه تعصرون، بكسر التاء والعين والصاد وشدها، وأصله تعتصرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r14.claim: Joseph interpreted the fat cows and green ears as fertile years, and the lean cows and dry ears as drought years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r14.anchor: تأول يوسف عليه السلام البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسين مخصبة، والعجاف واليابسات بسنين مجدبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r15.claim: After interpreting the dream, Joseph announced a blessed, abundant eighth year through revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r15.anchor: ثم بشرهم بعد الفراغ من تأويل الرؤيا بمجيء العام الثامن مباركا خصيبا كثير الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r16.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r16.claim: Qatada says God gave Joseph knowledge of an additional year; revelation specified the eighth year’s abundance, already expected after seven severe years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p286/r16.anchor: وعن قتادة: زاده الله علم سنة، والذي من جهة الوحي هو التفضيل بحال العام

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r1.claim: Yughāthu means people receive rain; ghayth itself means rain.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r2.claim: Yaʿṣirūn means pressing grapes or olives.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r2.anchor: {وفيه يعصرون} يعني: الأعناب والزيت. وقال أبو عبيدة (2) (يعصرون) : ينجون والعصرة النجاة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets yaʿṣirūn as being rescued; ʿaṣra means rescue.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r3.anchor:
*ولقد كان عصرة المنجود* (3)
أي: غياثا ومنجاة للمكروب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r4.speaker: شاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r4.claim: A poet calls rescue for a distressed person ʿaṣra, “relief,” supporting Abū ʿUbayda's reading.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p218#5/r4.anchor:
*ولقد كان عصرة المنجود* (3)
أي: غياثا ومنجاة للمكروب.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r1.claim: عام and سنة both mean year, but عام often suggests ease and fertility whereas سنة often suggests hardship and famine; the positive term signals the changed conditions from the preceding years.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r1.anchor: هو كالسنة لكن كثيرا ما يستعمل فيما فيه الرخاء والخصب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and most exegetes explain يغاث الناس as receiving rain, from the triliteral root غاث.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور فهو من غاث الثلاثي اليائي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r3.claim: Another explanation derives it from relief: God will succor them by lifting the hardships pressing upon them, using the fourth-form verb from غوث.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r3.anchor: أمدنا برفع المكاره حين أظلتنا فهو رباعي واوي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r4.claim: They will press products normally squeezed, such as grapes, sugarcane, olives, and sesame; explicit mention matters because rain does not ensure these crops as directly as grain, or because this special good news suits the king's own circumstances and makes his reading's second-person form apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r4.anchor: من العصر المعروف أي يعصرون ما من شأنه أي يعصر من العنب والقصب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the verb as milking; this can derive from pressing because milking squeezes the udder to release milk.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس تفسير ذلك بيحلبون وكأنه مأخوذ من العصر المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r6.claim: Repeating فيه can signal different times or kinds of benefit, enumerate the year's blessings, or emphasize that the preceding drought's rain was negligible beside this year's; the fronting of the phrase marks the focus, with rhyme also possible for the second occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p255#3/r6.anchor: المقام مقام تعداد منافع ذلك العام ولأجله قدم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد والأعرج وعيسى البصرة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r1.claim: Ja'far ibn Muhammad, al-Aʿraj, and ʿIsa of Basra read يعصرون as passive; ʿIsa also transmits a second-person passive reading, 'you will be delivered' from hardship, matching 'people will receive rain'.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r1.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما والأعرج وعيسى البصرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda and others take the active form as pressing in the sense of rescue; al-Bahr gives a related lexical sense of relief and cites Abu Zubayd's poem about Uthman as a refuge for the distressed.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r2.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة وغيره أخذ المبني للفاعل من العصر بمعنى النجاة أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munir understands the verb as receiving rain from a cloud whose time to be squeezed has come, with the preposition omitted or the verb carrying the sense of raining.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r3.anchor: معناه عصيرون من أعصرت السحابة عليهم أي حان وقت عصر الرياح لها لتمطر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r4.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari says عصر القوم means that a people received rain, which makes the reading apparent without a verbal supplement.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r4.anchor: وفي الصحاح عصر القوم أي أمطروا ومنه قراءة بعضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r5.speaker: النقاش
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash transmits a doubled form يعصّرون with a passive yā and kasra on ṣād, conveying abundance or intensity.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r5.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه قريء ( يعصرون ) بضم الياء وكسر الصاد وتشديدها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads تعصرون with a doubled consonant from an assimilated form of تعتصرون; it can mean squeezing fruit or being rescued.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( وفيه تعصرون ) بكسر التاء والعين والصاد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r7.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r7.claim: Qatada, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and others, and Ibn Abbas say God granted Joseph knowledge of this year's details by revelation; Al-Alusi treats revelation as the apparent source.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r7.anchor: كما أخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن قتادة علم آتاه الله تعالى علمه لم يكن فيما سئل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r8.claim: Joseph ends his answer to the king with the glad news; unlike his answer to the prisoners, where the prediction came first, this placement at the end highlights his excellence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r8.anchor: ولقد أتى عليه السلام بما يدل على فضله في آخر فتواه على عكس ما فعل أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r9.claim: A non-revelatory view says Joseph inferred that drought naturally ends in abundance or that God sends ease after hardship; Al-Alusi rejects it because the prophecy would be vague, especially in readings where mutual relief is described, which only revelation could establish.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r9.anchor: إن هذه البشارة منه عليه السلام لم تكن عن وحي بل لأن العادة جارية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports Joseph began testing the coming famine by preparing two portions for each man; when one man ate all of his, Joseph said that was the first day of the hard years.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r10.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن زيد بن أسلم أنه عليه السلام كان بعد ذلك يصنع لرجل طعام اثنين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r11.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r11.claim: Al-Balkhi uses the counselors' dismissal of the king's dream as confused dreams to challenge the rule that dreams occur according to their first interpretation; Al-Alusi replies with the hadith that a dream hangs on a bird's wing until interpreted, and says dismissing it as meaningless may not count as interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r11.anchor: واستدل البلخي بتأويله لذلك على بطلان قول من يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi restricts the dream rule to visions admitting several possible meanings: one interpretation is made and then comes to pass.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r12.anchor: إنه ينبغي أن يخص ذلك بما يحتمل من الرؤيا وجوها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r13.claim: The passage is also cited as evidence that an unbeliever can have a true dream; interpreters are advised not to ask at sunrise, sunset, or night, and some say a dream seen in sleep is its own interpretation. Al-Alusi finds many such claims opaque.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p256/r13.anchor: واستدلوا بذلك أيضا على صحة رؤيا الكافر وهو ظاهر وقد ذكروا للإستفتاء عن الرؤيا آدابا

MAJAZ:v1p312/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p312/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p312/r7.claim: Yaʿṣirūn means they are rescued by it; ʿaṣrah also means rescue, as in the line about the oppressed man.
MAJAZ:v1p312/r7.anchor:
«وفيه يعصرون» (49) أي به ينجون وهو من العصر وهى العصرة أيضا وهى المنجاة، قال:
ولقد كان عصرة المنجود

MAJAZ:v1p312/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p312/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p312/r8.claim: Labīd's line uses muʿṣir for rescue or refuge.
MAJAZ:v1p312/r8.anchor:
وقال لبيد:
فبات وأسرى القوم آخر ليلهم ... وما كان وقافا بغير معصر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r3.claim: The final year brings rain; alternatively, people are rescued from hardship, based on the idiom “I sought help and he helped me.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r3.anchor: {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس} أي: يمطرون، من الغيث: وهو المطر. وقيل: ينقذون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read تعصرون with تاء to continue the direct address; others use ياء to refer to the people, who press grapes, olives, and sesame for oil and enjoy abundance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: " تعصرون " بالتاء، لأن الكلام كله على الخطاب، وقرأ الآخرون بالياء ردا إلى الناس،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets يعصرون as being rescued from distress and drought; العصر can mean deliverance or refuge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p247#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: يعصرون أي ينجون من الكروب والجدب، والعصر والعصرة: المنجاة والملجأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r3.claim: The people will receive rain or be relieved from drought; they will press grapes and olives because fruit is plentiful, or milk their animals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r3.anchor: { ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس } يمطرون من الغيث أو يغاثون من القحط

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'you will press' by addressing the king's questioner; other readings are passive or active forms of giving relief, or derive from a cloud bringing rain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالتاء على تغليب المستفتي، وقرىء على بناء المفعول

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r5.claim: The final year is good news: fat cows and green ears mean fertile years, lean cows and dry ears mean famine, and the former being swallowed means stored abundance will be consumed; Joseph may know this by revelation or inference from God's custom of relief after hardship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:48-50/r5.anchor: وهذه بشارة بشرهم بها بعد أن أول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخصبة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r4.claim: The following year is a full twelve months; calling it ʿām signals that its coming relief is known and controlled by God alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r4.anchor: والتعبير به دون مرادفاته إشارة إلى أنه من المعلوم أنه لا يقدر عليها إلا الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r5.claim: “People will be given rain” may derive from ghayth, rain, or “people will be relieved” from ghawth, deliverance; the first has three- and four-letter forms, the second only four-letter forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r5.anchor: ففي الأول يجوز بناءه من ثلاثي ومن رباعين يقال غاث الله الأرض وأغاثها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r6.claim: “They will press” means extracting the juices and essences of things; pressing marks the transition from drought to fertility.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p52/r6.anchor: { يعصرون } أي يخرجون عصارات الأشياء وخلاصاتها

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the final year brings rain and people press grapes, oil, and other fruits.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {عام فيه يغاث الناس} يقول: يصيبهم فيه غيث

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah glosses يعصرون as milking.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {وفيه يعصرون} يحتلبون

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r5.claim: Qatadah says rain comes in that year and people press fruits, grapes, and olives amid renewed fertility.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r5.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس} قال: يغاث الناس بالمطر

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r6.claim: Qatadah says Joseph gave them knowledge of one additional year beyond the years they asked about.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r6.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام} الآية قال: زادهم يوسف عليه السلام علم سنة

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God taught Joseph to volunteer an unasked-for forecast: rain, sesame pressed for oil, grapes for wine, and olives for oil.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام} قال: أخبرهم بشيء لم يسألوه عنه

DURR-FULL:v4p546/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the year of relief as rain and says people press their grapes.
DURR-FULL:v4p546/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه {فيه يغاث الناس} قال: بالمطر {وفيه يعصرون} قال: يعصرون أعنابهم

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says people receive rain and press oil in the year of relief.
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك - رضي الله عنه - {فيه يغاث الناس} قال: يغاث الناس بالمطر {وفيه يعصرون} قال: الزيت

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r2.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Abbas uses the second-person form taʿṣirūn and means that people milk.
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r2.anchor: عن علي بن طلحة - رضي الله عنه - قال: كان ابن عباس - رضي الله عنه - يقرأ / وفيه تعصرون / بالتاء يعني تحتلبون

DURR-FULL:v4p547/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عبيد الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r3.claim: A reciter reads with second-person forms; the note explains relief as rain and cites the verse about water poured down from the rain clouds.
DURR-FULL:v4p547/r3.anchor: عن عيسى بن عبيد عن عيسى بن عمير الثقفي - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعته يقرأ / فيه يغاث الناس وفيه تعصرون / بالتاء

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r1.claim: The year in which people receive aid is a year of rainfall.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس قوله : ثم ياتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون يقول : يصيبهم فيه غيث

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r2.claim: People are aided by rain in that year.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r2.anchor: ثنا قتادة قوله : ثم ياتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس قال : يغاث الناس بالمطر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r3.claim: “They press” refers to pressing grapes and oil.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون يقول : الاعناب والدهن

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r4.claim: People press grapes, olives, and other fruits in that year.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وفيه يعصرون . يقول : يعصرون فيه العنب ، ويعصرون فيه الزيت ، ويعصرون من كل الثمرات

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r5.claim: In the fertile year people press fruits, grapes, and olives; this was knowledge God gave Joseph beyond what he had been asked.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r5.anchor: ثنا قتادة : وفيه يعصرون الثمار والاعناب والزيتون من الخصب ، وهذا علم اتاه الله علمه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation of “they press” is that people milk animals.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قول الله : عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون قال : يحلبون

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r7.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r7.claim: Ibn Umar's recitation reads “they are given rain”; the phrase means relief and rainfall, as in the verse about water poured from rain clouds.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2154#2/r7.anchor: سمعت عيسى بن عمر الثقفي ، يقرا : فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون يعني : الغياث والمطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.claim: In the dream's interpretation, cows represent agricultural years, fatness fertility, leanness drought, and ears of grain provisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#2/r1.anchor: فالبقرات لسنين الزراعة ، لأن البقرة تتخذ للإثمار . والسمن رمز للخصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r8.claim: The promise of a year of relief and pressing produce brings comfort and hope after the discouraging forecast, reflecting God's pattern of ease after hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p286#3/r8.anchor: فهو بشارة وإدخال المسرة والأمل بعد الكلام المؤيس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r2.claim: The phrase يغاث الناس may derive from rain, meaning people will receive rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r2.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وجمهور المفسرين، أي يمطرون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r3.claim: Alternatively, it can mean God relieves them; ghawth is relief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r3.anchor: من أغاثهم الله، أذا فرج عنهم، ومنه الغوث وهو الفرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r4.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAsim read yaʿṣirūn; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the address form taʿṣirūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r4.anchor: بفتح الياء وكسر الصاد، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r5.claim: Most interpreters take the verb as pressing produce such as olives, grapes, sugar cane, sesame, and radish; milking is also pressing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r5.anchor: هي من عصر النباتات كالزيتون والعنب والقصب والسمسم والفجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r6.claim: It is reported that people could not press anything during the drought years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r6.anchor: وروي أنهم لم يعصروا شيئا مدة الجدب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda and others derive the verb from ʿaṣra, refuge or relief, rather than pressing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r7.anchor: ذلك مأخوذ من العصرة والعصر وهو الملجأ ومنه قول أبي زبيد في عثمان رضي الله عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r8.claim: Poetry by Abu Zubayd, ʿAdi ibn Zayd, Ibn Muqbil, and Labid uses ʿaṣr and related forms to mean refuge or a place to take shelter.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r9.speaker: الأعرج وعيسى وجعفر بن محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r9.claim: These readers use the passive yuʿṣarūn, which may mean given relief, or squeezed by clouds; Ibn al-Mustanir takes it to mean rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r9.anchor: أي يؤتون بعصرة ويحتمل أن يكون من عصرات السحاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r10.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r10.claim: Al-Naqqash records a reading that takes the word as squeezing moisture or similar liquid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r11.claim: Al-Tabari strongly rejects deriving the word from refuge, but the author says he gives no proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p251/r11.anchor: ورد الطبري على من جعل اللفظة من العصرة ردا كثيرا بغير حجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r1.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r1.claim: One explanation for the masculine “that” referring to feminine years is that the number seven has no feminine marker and resembles a masculine form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن السبع مؤنثه ولا علامة للتأنيث في لفظها فأشبهت المذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi supports the first explanation with a verse where masculine grammar follows a feminine noun lacking a feminine marker.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r3.claim: Muqatil says “that” refers to the drought, rather than to the years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r3.anchor: والثاني أن ذلك إشارة إلى الجدب وهذا قول مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r4.claim: Qatada says God gave Joseph knowledge of the abundant year, which the questioners had not asked about.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r4.anchor: قال قتادة زاده الله علم عام لم يسألوه عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “people are given relief” as rain coming to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r5.anchor: أحدهما يصيبهم الغيث قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi interprets it as people receiving relief through abundance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r7.claim: These readers use the third-person plural in “they press”; Hamza and al-Kisa'i address the people who asked for interpretation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم يعصرون بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r8.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وقتادة والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r8.claim: The first interpretation of yaʿṣirūn is pressing grapes, olives, or fruits; al-Awfi transmits it from Ibn Abbas, and Qatada and most commentators agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r8.anchor: أحدها يعصرون العنب والزيت والثمرات رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال قتادة والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r9.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to interpret it as milking; a cited poem uses the verb for milking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r9.anchor: والثاني يعصرون بمعنى يحتلبون رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda gives “they are rescued” from the root meaning rescue or refuge, supported by poetry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r10.anchor: والثالث ينجون وهو من العصر والعصر النجاء والعصرة المنجاة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن ابن أحمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r11.claim: Another view from Abu Ubayda is “they obtain what they desire,” supported by Ibn Ahmar's poem.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r11.anchor: والرابع يصيبون ما يحبون روي عن أبي عبيدة أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r12.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r12.claim: Some grammarians say the people are given abundant produce, making their lives prosperous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r12.anchor: والخامس يعطون ويفضلون لسعة عيشهم رواه ابن الأنباري عن بعض أهل الغة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r13.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads the verb passively; al-Zajjaj says this means they receive rain, by analogy with the rain-bearing clouds verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p233#3/r13.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير يعصرون بضم الياء وفتح الصاد وقال الزجاج أراد يمطرون

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r1.claim: يُغاث may derive from الغوث (relief), with quadriliteral أغاثنا الله.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r2.claim: Or it derives from الغيث (rain): غيثت البلاد means it rained, and غاثنا الله is triliteral.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r3.claim: A Bedouin woman uses غثنا ما شئنا to mean “we got whatever rain we wished.”

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r4.claim: The two brothers read تعصرون in second person; others read يعصرون in third person, each matching a preceding addressee or absent subject.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r5.claim: The clearest sense of يعصرون is pressing grapes, olives, or the like.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r6.claim: Another sense is milking an udder.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r7.claim: A third sense is rescue, from العصرة; Abu Zubayd's verse calls Uthman a refuge for the distressed.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r8.claim: Rescue fits the preceding يُغاث: عصره means he saved him.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r9.claim: Jaafar ibn Muhammad and al-Araj read passive يعصرون with ya; Isa of Basra reads passive تعصرون with ta.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r10.claim: One passive reading means rescued, which al-Zamakhshari says matches the relief in يُغاث.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r11.speaker: قطرب
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r11.claim: Qutrub instead derives it from cloud-rain, as in 78:14; al-Zamakhshari explains the transitivity by ellipsis or metaphor.
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r11.anchor: قاله قطرب أنها من الإعصار، وهو إمطار

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r12.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads تَعَصَّرون, deriving from تعتصرون by assimilation and successive vowel matching.

SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r13.speaker: النقاش
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r13.claim: Al-Naqqash transmits يُعَصِّرون with doubled صاد as an intensive form; these readings can mean pressing, milking, or rescue.
SAMIN-DURR:12:49/r13.anchor: ونقل النقاش قراءة " يعصرون " بضم الياء

SAMIN-DURR:12:49#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:49#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:49#2/r1.claim: An anonymous verse uses اعتصاري to mean “my rescue,” supporting the deliverance sense of عصر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r2.claim: After the seven drought years, another year brings rain and flourishing crops; people press their usual products such as oil and sweet syrup.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r2.anchor: ويعصر الناس ما كانوا يعصرون على عادتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p393/r3.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha transmits from Ibn Abbas that 'they press' means they milk animals.

JISHUMI:v5p3652/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r5.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read تعصرون addressing the listeners, in parallel with قدمتم; the other readers use third-person yaʾ for the people.
JISHUMI:v5p3652/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: تعصرون بالتاء على الخطاب لقوله: قدمتم لهن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r5.claim: Yuʿṣirūn can mean people press grapes, olives, or sesame, or milk livestock; a passive reading means they are rescued, and an active sense means they rescue themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r5.anchor: يعصرون } بالياء والتاء : يعصرون العنب والزيتون والسمسم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r6.claim: Yuʿṣirūn may instead mean that they receive rain, with either a verb meaning rain or an omitted preposition understood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r6.anchor: وقيل { يعصرون } يمطرون ، من أعصرت السحابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r9.claim: The end of a famine implies some fertility in general, but the detailed promise that people will receive relief and press produce in that year can only be known by revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p449/r9.anchor: وقوله { فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون } تفصيل لحال العام ، وذلك لا يعلم إلا بالوحي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r27.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r27.claim: يغاث الناس means that people will receive rain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r27.anchor: يغاثون بنزول الغيث , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r28.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r28.claim: يغاث الناس may mean that people receive abundant produce.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r29.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r29.claim: يعصرون means pressing grapes and olives because fruit is plentiful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r29.anchor: يعصرون العنب والزيتون من خصب الثمار , قاله مجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r30.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r30.claim: يعصرون may mean bringing livestock from abundant pasture.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r30.anchor: أي فيه يجلبون المواشي من خصب المراعي , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r31.speaker: عيسى بن عمر الثقفي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r31.claim: يعصرون may describe clouds being pressed into abundant rain, linked to the rain from the clouds in 78:14.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r31.anchor: كثرة المطر , من قوله تعالى ^ { وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا } ^ [ النبأ : 14 ] . قاله عيسى بن عمر الثقفي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r32.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r32.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj interpret يعصرون as being rescued, deriving it from عصرة meaning deliverance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p42/r32.anchor: مأخوذ من العصرة وهي المنجاة , قاله أبو عبيدة والزجاج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r1.claim: A cited poem says a thirsty person calls without receiving help and calls him rescued, supporting the deliverance sense of عصرة.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r1.anchor: صاديا يستغيث غير مغاث … ولقد كان عصرة المنجود

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r2.claim: يعصرون may mean improving and prospering, as in the poetic usage يعصر فينا for treating us well.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r2.anchor: تحسنون وتفضلون , ومنه قول الشاعر : لو كان في أملاكنا ملك … يعصر فينا مثل ما تعصر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r3.claim: The final good-year statement may be prophetic information granted by God, independent of interpreting the dream.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p45/r3.anchor: وهذا القول من يوسف غير متعلق بتأويل الرؤيا

MUQATIL:12:48-51/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r2.claim: After the drought comes a year of rain in which Egyptians press grapes and oil; Muqatil says this is Joseph's statement, not part of the dream.
MUQATIL:12:48-51/r2.anchor: { عام فيه يغاث الناس } ، يعني أهل مصر بالمطر، { وفيه يعصرون } [آية: 49] العنب، والزيت من الخصب،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r1.claim: The abundant year comes after the fourteen preceding years; people will receive relief, either because their pleas are answered or because it rains.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r1.anchor: أى من بعد اربع عشرة سنة عام ﴿ فيه يغاث الناس ﴾ من الغوث أى يجاب مستغيثهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r2.claim: In that year people press grapes, olives, and sesame into drinks and oils; Hamza reads the verb with the stated variant.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r2.anchor: العنب الزيتون والسمسم فيتخذون الأشربة والادهان تعصرون حمزة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r3.claim: Joseph interprets the fat cows and green ears as plentiful years, the lean cows and dry ears as famine years, and, by revelation, announces a blessed eighth year of abundant good.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p192#3/r3.anchor: فاول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب والعجاف واليابسات بسنين مجدبة

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r3.claim: With yāʾ, yaʿṣirūn means they will press oil and grapes; with yāʾ in the passive sense, yuʿṣarūn means they will receive rain; taʿṣirūn may mean pressing or escaping distress through abundance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r3.anchor: فمن قال وفيه يعصرون بالياء أي يأتي العام بعد أربع عشرة سنة

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r4.speaker: عدي بن زيد
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r4.claim: ʿAdī ibn Zayd’s poem uses iʿtiṣār for relief through water, supporting the interpretation of rescue or abundance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r4.anchor:
قال عدي بن زيد:
لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق

ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r5.claim: A person may be said to be in ʿaṣr when safely inside a stronghold beyond reach.
ZAJJAJ:v3p113/r5.anchor: ويقال: فلان في عصر وفي عصر، إذا كان في حصن

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r1.claim: The plentiful year was not in the king's dream; Joseph knew it through unseen knowledge granted by God.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r1.anchor: هذا خبر من يوسف عليه السلام عما لم يكن في رؤيا الملك، ولكنه من علم الغيب الذي آتاه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r2.claim: Qatāda says God gave Joseph knowledge of an extra year they had not asked about, displaying his merit and knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: زاده الله علم سنة لم يسألوه عنها إظهارا لفضله

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r3.claim: Yughāthu means people receive rain, whether derived from relief or from ghawth; the commentary distinguishes the related forms for seeking aid, relief, and rainfall.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they will press grapes and produce oil; al-Bukhārī records this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعصرون الأعناب والدهن ذكره البخاري

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that people will press grapes into wine, sesame into oil, and olives into oil.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r5.anchor: يعصرون العنب خمرا والسمسم دهنا، والزيتون زيتا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the verb as milking livestock, which would indicate abundant vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r6.anchor: وقيل: أراد حلب الألبان لكثرتها ويدل ذلك على كثرة النبات

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r7.claim: A further interpretation reads the verb as being saved or delivered, from ʿuṣra meaning refuge; Abū ʿUbayda likewise defines ʿaṣr and ʿuṣra as refuge, supported by Abū Zubayd's poetry using ʿaṣra.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r7.anchor: وقيل: «يعصرون» أي ينجون وهو من العصرة، وهي المنجاة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r8.speaker: أبو الغوث
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r8.claim: Abū al-Ghawth glosses the verb as exploiting produce, from pressing grapes; iʿtaṣartu mālahu means extracting wealth from someone's hand.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r9.speaker: عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r9.claim: ʿĪsā reads taʿṣirūn with a damma on tāʾ and fatḥa on ṣād, meaning you are rained upon, as in 78:14; another reading with kasra on ṣād has the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:49/r9.anchor: وقرأ عيسى «تعصرون» بضم التاء وفتح الصاد، ومعناه: تمطرون

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.claim: The first seven years are fertile and the next seven years are drought, as indicated by the dream; the forecast of a further abundant year came through revelation, and Qatada says God granted Joseph knowledge of that year.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#2/r9.anchor: وعن قتادة زاده الله علم سنة

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r1.claim: The dream indicated the shift from drought to fertility, but the detailed forecast that people would receive relief and press produce came only through revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r1.anchor: أما تفصيل الحال فيه ، وهو قوله : { فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون } لا يعلم إلا بالوحي

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit explains يغاث as rain falling on the land; it can also mean that people are rescued from the distress of drought.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن السكيت يقال : غاث الله البلاد يغيثها

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r3.claim: يعصرون may mean they press sesame for oil, grapes for wine, and olives for oil, or milk their livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r3.anchor: أي يعصرون السمسم دهنا والعنب خمرا والزيتون زيتا

RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r4.claim: A reading from the root عصَر can mean rescue, while another derives the verb from clouds bringing rain, as in 78:14.
RAZI-FULL:v18p120#3/r4.anchor: وقرىء { يعصرون } من عصره إذا نجاه

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ASAD-NOTES:12:47#n48/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:47#n48/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:47#n48/r1.claim: Yughath can mean that the people receive rain or are delivered from distress; either reading fits Egypt's crops, which depend on Nile floods fed by rainfall upstream.
ASAD-NOTES:12:47#n48/r1.anchor: depending on whether one connects the verbal form yughath with either of the infinitive nouns ghayth ("rain") or ghawth ("deliverance from distress")

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.claim: Joseph’s interpretation covers the next fifteen years of Egypt’s agricultural cycle.
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r1.anchor: what would happen during the next fifteen years of Egypt’s agrarian cycle

STUDYQURAN:12:47/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r5.claim: The final year would bring abundant bounty; pressing oil and wine signaled that food was plentiful again.
STUDYQURAN:12:47/r5.anchor: the pressing of oil and wine is an indication that there would be food in abundance once again; cf. Genesis 41:25–36.

TAB-FULL:v13p194/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r1.claim: The forecast of a final year of relief was not part of the king's dream; God taught Yusuf this unseen knowledge as a sign of his prophethood and truthfulness.
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r1.anchor: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

TAB-FULL:v13p194/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r2.claim: Qatada says God gave Yusuf knowledge of an additional year about which the people had not asked.
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " ثم زاده الله علم سنة لم يسألوه عنها، فقال: {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49]

TAB-FULL:v13p194/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r3.claim: Yugāth al-nās means people receive rain and relief from rainfall.

TAB-FULL:v13p194/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p194/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses the year in which people receive relief as a year of rain.

TAB-FULL:v13p195/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities explain 'they press' as pressing grapes, sesame, oil, olives, and other fruits in the fertile year.
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49] السمسم دهنا، والعنب خمرا، والزيتون زيتا

TAB-FULL:v13p195/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r2.claim: A second interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas takes the verb as milking; a reading with tā' makes the audience the ones who milk.
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، " {وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49] قال: فيه يحلبون

TAB-FULL:v13p195/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r3.claim: Regional readers transmit ya' for people pressing produce and ta' for directly addressing the audience; al-Tabari accepts either established reading because they agree in meaning.
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r3.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك أن لقارئه الخيار في قراءته بأي القراءتين الأخريين شاء

TAB-FULL:v13p195/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r4.claim: A reported ya' reading meaning 'they are rained upon' is not acceptable because it conflicts with the established readings of the regional readers.
TAB-FULL:v13p195/r4.anchor: وقرأه بعضهم: «وفيه يعصرون» بمعنى: يمطرون، وهذه قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لخلافها

TAB-FULL:v13p197/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r1.claim: Al-Tabari rejects interpreting ya'sirun as escaping drought through rain by analogy with al-'asr meaning rescue; poetry cannot outweigh the unanimous interpretation of the Companions and Successors.
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r1.anchor: وذلك تأويل يكفي من الشهادة على خطئه، خلافه قول جميع أهل العلم من الصحابة والتابعين

TAB-FULL:v13p197/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r2.claim: The interpretation transmitted through al-Faraj ibn Fadala from Ali ibn Abi Talha has no sound meaning because it conflicts with known Arabic and Ibn Abbas's usage.
TAB-FULL:v13p197/r2.anchor: وأما القول الذي روى الفرج بن فضالة عن علي بن أبي طلحة، فقول لا معنى له، لأنه خلاف المعروف من كلام العرب

TABATABAI:12:46-49/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r10.claim: Yughath may mean that people are helped through relief from hardship, or that they receive rain; the next phrase about pressing makes the rain sense more apt.
TABATABAI:12:46-49/r10.anchor: كان معناه ينصرون فيه من قبل الله سبحانه بكشف الكربة

TABATABAI:12:49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r1.claim: The rain sense of yughath fits the reference to pressing; the claim that aid is more natural is unpersuasive except under a passive reading of yaʿsirun, they are rained upon.
TABATABAI:12:49/r1.anchor: وهذا المعنى الثاني أنسب بالنظر إلى قوله بعده

TABATABAI:12:49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r2.claim: An objection that Egypt’s fertility depends on Nile flooding rather than rain fails because the floodwaters are supplied by rain in Sudan.
TABATABAI:12:49/r2.anchor: رد عليه بأن الفيضان نفسه لا يكون إلا بالمطر الذي يمده في مجاريه من بلاد السودان

TABATABAI:12:49/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r3.speaker: لسان العرب
TABATABAI:12:49/r3.claim: The lexicon also defines ghayth as vegetation grown from rainwater, a sense that fits the following mention of pressing.
TABATABAI:12:49/r3.anchor: قال في لسان العرب والغيث الكلاء ينبت من ماء السماء

TABATABAI:12:49/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r4.claim: Pressing can mean extracting juice or oil from fruit and plants, and some interpret it as milking livestock.
TABATABAI:12:49/r4.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد بالعصر الحلب أي يحلبون ضروع أنعامهم كما فسره بعضهم به

TABATABAI:12:49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r5.claim: The final year brings crops, rain, or divine relief and abundant produce or milk; the phrasing implies plentiful blessing for people and livestock.
TABATABAI:12:49/r5.anchor: وفيه كناية عن توفر النعمة عليهم وعلى أنعامهم ومواشيهم

TABATABAI:12:49/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r6.speaker: البيضاوي
TABATABAI:12:49/r6.claim: Al-Baydawi treats the final fertile year as glad tidings beyond the interpretation of fat and lean cows; Joseph may have known it through revelation, the expected end of drought, or God’s custom of easing hardship.
TABATABAI:12:49/r6.anchor: ولعله علم ذلك بالوحى أو بأن انتهاء الجدب بالخصب أو بأن السنة الإلهية

TABATABAI:12:49/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r7.speaker: صاحب المنار
TABATABAI:12:49/r7.claim: The Manar author says the final year’s exceptional abundance is extra information not entailed by the dream and therefore known to Joseph through revelation.
TABATABAI:12:49/r7.anchor: وقال صاحب المنار في تفسيره في الآية والمراد أن هذا العام

TABATABAI:12:49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.claim: The author says interpreters wrongly treat the dream as a forecast of seven fertile then seven barren years; Joseph instead states the required policy for surviving the anticipated famine.
TABATABAI:12:49/r8.anchor: لم يبن كلامه على أساس إخبارهم بما سيستقبلهم من السنين السبع المخصبة ثم السنين السبع المجدبة

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r6.claim: The final year is inferred from the repeated seven: after the seven difficult years people need not exert themselves to manage sowing and reserves.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أنه عليه السلام استفاده من عدد السبع الذي تكرر في البقرات السمان والعجاف

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r1.claim: Joseph shifts from addressing the group directly to saying people will receive rain or aid and press produce, indicating they will no longer need to manage their livelihoods.
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r1.anchor: ولعله لهذه الثلاثة غير السياق فقال

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r2.speaker: صاحب المنار
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r2.claim: The Manar author argues that the unusually specific final-year forecast cannot come from the dream and must come from revelation.
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r2.anchor: أن هذا التخصيص لم يعرفه يوسف عليه السلام إلا بوحي من الله لا مقابل له في رؤيا الملك

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r4.claim: Rain, fodder growth, or milking livestock best fits the imagery of fat and lean cows, explaining the specific mention of rain and pressing.
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r4.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر أيضا أن الأنسب أن يكون المراد

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.claim: A report says Joseph stockpiled the harvests, sold food during famine first for money, then valuables, livestock, servants, property, and land, and finally for people’s freedom; he then freed the Egyptians and restored their possessions and kingship.
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r2.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يقول وأقبل يوسف على جمع الطعام في السبع السنين المخصبة فكبسه في الخزائن

TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.claim: The author omits many similar reports about the famine economy because most do not directly serve the interpretation of these verses.
TABATABAI:12:43-57#2/r3.anchor: والروايات في هذا المقام كثيرة أغلبها غير مرتبطة بغرض تفسير الآيات ولذلك تركنا نقلها

TABATABAI:78:13-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r8.speaker: جعفر الصادق
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r8.claim: Al-Sadiq reads yuʿṣirūn in the rain year as “they are rained upon,” citing 78:14; the author identifies the verb as passive and al-muʿṣirāt as clouds that rain.
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r8.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون بالياء يمطرون

TABATABAI:78:13-14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r9.speaker: علي بن معمر
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r9.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits a similar explanation from Ali ibn Maʿmar and his father, and Qummi transmits it from Ali.
TABATABAI:78:13-14/r9.anchor: وروى العياشي مثل الحديث عن علي بن معمر عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABRISI:12:43-49/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r7.speaker: جعفر بن محمد، الأعرج، عيسى بن عمر
TABRISI:12:43-49/r7.claim: These readers use a form of يعصرون with a damma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ṣād.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r7.anchor: قرأ هو والأعرج وعيسى بن عمر وفيه يعصرون بياء مضمومة وصاد مفتوحة

TABRISI:12:43-49/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49/r9.claim: يعصرون can mean pressing oil, water, or juice from produce, fitting the return of prosperity after a drought; some say they had pressed neither oil nor wine for fourteen years.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r9.anchor: من العصر الذي يراد به الضغط الذي يلحق ما فيه دهن أو ماء نحو الزيتون

TABRISI:12:43-49/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r10.speaker: ابن مقبل، أبو زبيد الطائي، أبو عبيدة، لبيد
TABRISI:12:43-49/r10.claim: Another sense of العصر is seeking refuge or means of rescue; Ibn Muqbil, Abu Zubayd, Abu ʿUbayda, and Labid provide poetic evidence for rescue or escape.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r10.anchor: وهذا يمكن أن يكون تأويل الآية عليه لأن من المتأولين من يحكى أنهم لم يعصروا

TABRISI:12:43-49/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49/r11.claim: The yāʾ form refers to the previously mentioned people; the tāʾ form addresses the people who requested interpretation, and may include others as well.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r11.anchor: فأما من قال: يعصرون بالياء فإنه جعل الفاعلين الناس

TABRISI:12:43-49/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r12.speaker: علي
TABRISI:12:43-49/r12.claim: ʿAli rejects a reading that would imply people press wine during the famine year and directs the reader to a form meaning they receive rain after famine.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r12.anchor: فقال ويحك وأي شيء يعصرون أيعصرون الخمر

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r11.claim: Ghawth is help that meets an urgent need and removes harm; ghayth is rain arriving when it is needed.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r11.anchor: والغوث هو نفع يأتي على شدة حاجة ينفي المضرة ومنه الغيث المطر

TABRISI:12:47-49/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:47-49/r10.claim: The final year brings rain and relief; يَغاث may refer either to rainfall or to rescue from drought.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r10.anchor: يمطر الناس من الغيث. وقيل: يغاثون من الغوث والغياث

TABRISI:12:47-49/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:47-49/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
TABRISI:12:47-49/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say people will press fruits such as grapes, olives, and sesame in the prosperous year.
TABRISI:12:47-49/r11.anchor: الثمار التي تعصر في الخصب كالعنب والزيت والسمسم عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r1.claim: يَعصرون may mean they escape famine by resorting to a means of rescue; the verse is illustrated by a poetic image of thirst and reliance on water.
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r1.anchor: لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق كنت كالغصان بالماء اعتصاري

TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r2.claim: Yusuf's forecast of the prosperous year goes beyond the king's dream and question, and is knowledge of the unseen God disclosed as a sign of prophethood.
TABRISI:12:43-49#3/r2.anchor: وهذا القول من يوسف إخبار بما لم يسألوه منه ولم يكن في رؤيا الملك

THALABI:v5p227/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r5.claim: The final favorable year was not in the king’s dream; God gave Joseph knowledge of an extra year, as Qatada says.
THALABI:v5p227/r5.anchor: وهذا خبر من يوسف (عليه السلام) عما لم يكن في رؤيا الملك، ولكنه من علم الغيب

THALABI:v5p227/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p227/r6.claim: Qatada says God disclosed one additional year to Joseph beyond what the king asked him to interpret.
THALABI:v5p227/r6.anchor: كما قال قتادة: زاده الله علم سنة لم يسألوه عنها

THALABI:v5p227/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p227/r7.claim: Yugāthu can mean people receive rain, or are relieved and aided; the rain is called ghayth.
THALABI:v5p227/r7.anchor: فيه يغاث الناس أي يمطرون بالغيث وهو المطر، وقيل: يغاثون

THALABI:v5p227/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r8.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v5p227/r8.claim: Kufa readers except Asim read taʿṣirūn in the second person because the surrounding speech addresses the people; others read yaʿṣirūn referring to them.
THALABI:v5p227/r8.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا عاصما تعصرون، بالتاء لأن الكلام كله بالخطاب، وقرأ الباقون بالياء

THALABI:v5p227/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p227/r9.claim: Most commentators say they will press grapes, olives, and sesame; Ibn Abbas instead says they will milk animals.
THALABI:v5p227/r9.anchor: وروى الفرج بن فضالة عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: تعصرون تحلبون

THALABI:v5p227/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p227/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda takes yaʿṣirūn to mean escape drought and distress, since ʿaṣr can mean refuge; Abu Zubayd’s poem supports that sense.
THALABI:v5p227/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ينجون من الجدب والكرب، والعصر: المنجى والملجأ

THALABI:v5p227/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p227/r11.speaker: عيسى بن الأعرج
THALABI:v5p227/r11.claim: Isa ibn al-Aʿraj reads the verb passively, explaining that people will be rained upon; he links it with the rain from the clouds.
THALABI:v5p227/r11.anchor: يقرأها فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون، برفع الياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Joseph's interpretation came from knowledge God had taught him or direct revelation; the prediction of an unasked-for abundant year supports direct revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p136/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في أن جواب يوسف كان من علمه أو بوحي من الله تعالى؟ فذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أنه بنى على ما علمه الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r1.claim: The prediction of the abundant year was not part of the king's question, so it could only have come through revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬7): هذا العام لم يعلمه إلا بالوحي من أجل أنه لم يدخل في سؤال السائل؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r2.claim: Qatāda says God gave Joseph knowledge of a year the king had not asked about.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r2.anchor: قال # قتادة (¬1): زاده الله علم عام لم يسألوه عنه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī takes ذلك to refer to the seven years, since سبع has no feminine marker in its form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r3.anchor: من قبل أنها لا علامة للتأنيث في لفظها، كقوله {السماء منفطر به} [المزمل: 18] هذا مذهب الكلبي (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r4.claim: Muqātil takes ذلك to refer instead to the drought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r4.anchor: ومذهب مقاتل (¬4) أن (ذلك) إشارة إلى الجدب.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r5.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt explains يغاث as rain falling on the land, so the people receive rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r5.anchor: قال ابن السكيت (¬5): يقال: غاث الله البلاد يغيثها غيثا، وهي إذا نزل بها الغيث.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r6.claim: Alternatively, يغاث means the people are rescued from the distress of famine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p138/r6.anchor: فعلى هذا (يغاث الناس) معناه يمطرون، ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم: أغاثه الله، إذا أنقذه من كرب أو غم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r1.claim: The people would press sesame into oil, grapes into wine, and olives into oil, signaling that famine had ended and prosperity returned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r1.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس (¬6) ومجاهد (¬7) وقتادة (¬8) وأكثر المفسرين (¬9)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets يعصرون as escaping distress: العصر, العصرة, and المعتصر can mean refuge, supported by Arabic poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬1): يعصرون تفسيره ينجون من العصر وهو المنحاة، ومثله العصرة والمعتصر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq also allows “they are rescued from hardship and find refuge in prosperity,” citing the line about seeking refuge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r3.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق (¬1) أيضا هذا القول فقال: وإن شئت كان على تأويل ينجون من البلاء ويعتصمون بالخصب،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayd takes يعصرون to mean obtaining what they desire, supported by Ibn Aḥmar's verse about taking from life's branches.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد (¬3): يعصرون يعني به يصيبون ما يحبون، ويأخذون ما يشتهون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r5.claim: In al-Wālibī's report, يعصرون means milking; Aḥmad b. ʿUbayd agrees, linking it to abundant livestock and fertile years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس (¬6) في رواية الوالبي: يعصرون يحلبون. وإلى هذا ذهب أحمد بن عبيد (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r6.claim: A language scholar cited by Ibn al-Anbārī says يعصرون means giving generously and granting gifts; al-Azharī reports this sense from Abū ʿUbayd and Abū ʿUbayda.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r6.anchor: وروى ابن الأنباري (¬3) عن بعض أصحاب المعاني قال: تفسير يعصرون: يفضلون ويعطون ويحسنون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī prefers the first two senses, pressing produce and escaping hardship; no oil or wine was pressed in famine years, unlike prosperous years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p139/r7.anchor: واختار أبو علي الفارسي (¬6) القولين الأولين فقال: قوله: {يعصرون} يحتمل أمرين:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r5.claim: The final year will bring rain and abundant harvests, letting people press oil from sesame, wine from grapes, and oil from olives.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:47-50/r5.anchor: يمطرون ويخصبون حتى يعصروا من السمسم الدهن

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:49/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:49/r1.claim: Joseph predicts a further abundant year in which God helps people and they press grapes, dates, olives, and sesame for juice and oil; this good year is not signaled in the dream but revealed by God, showing dreams should be interpreted by qualified people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:49/r1.anchor: Kralın rüyasında bu bolluk yılına dair herhangi bir işaret yoktur. Hz. Yûsuf, Allah’ın verdiği bilgiye dayanarak bunu onlara müjdelemiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph also promised a year after the drought when God answers people's pleas, sends abundant rain, and yields a large grape harvest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He will send down abundant rain and they will get a thumping crop of grapes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Some interpreters understand yugāth as rain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some people have interpreted the word #!#.ﻐﺎث as rain.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The literal sense is seeking help, which portrays drought's full effects; rain is a consequential translation rather than the word's literal meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: By taking the word in its literal meaning of “seeking help”, a comprehensive picture of the all-embracing affects of drought on people is portrayed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The extraordinary year is one in which people cry out and plead with God until their pleas are answered.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: people will cry out and be forced to plead and beg the Almighty until finally their pleadings will be answered.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hardship drives even extreme polytheists and disbelievers to call on the one God and forget their imagined deities, as the Qur'an says.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the most extreme polytheists and disbelievers cry out for help from the one God and forget their hypothetical deities

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph guided Egypt through the drought, winning the admiration of everyone from the king to ordinary people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This period of drought was passed by the people of Egypt under the guidance of Joseph (sws). This made everyone from the king to the masses his great admirers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Yaʿṣirūn also has a consequential sense of abundant rain and productive grape vines; mentioning grape pressing subtly suits the king's wine-server.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The creepers of grapes will become very productive. People will profusely squeeze grapes.

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.claim: Al-Qummī reports the king’s dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears with dry ones; the cupbearer recalled it after a time, and Joseph interpreted seven plentiful years, seven famine years, then rain.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r5.anchor: ثم إن الملك رأى رؤيا فقال لوزرائه إني رأيت في نومي سبع بقرات سمان

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the revealed wording is “what you bring near for them” and interprets the following year as one in which people receive rain.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r7.anchor: قال الصادق عليه السلام إنما نزل ما قربتم لهن ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس

TABATABAI:12:56-57/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r8.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r8.claim: When a man recited “they press” actively, ʿAlī corrected him: the verse means they are rained upon, not that they press wine, as 78:14 confirms.
TABATABAI:12:56-57/r8.anchor: فقال ويحك أي شيء يعصرون يعصرون الخمر؟

TABATABAI:12:56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reads “they are rained upon” passively and takes yughāth from rain rather than rescue; al-ʿAyyāshī transmits the same interpretation.
TABATABAI:12:56/r3.anchor: إنما نزلت وفيه يعصرون أي يمطرون، أي بالبناء للمفعول ومنه يعلم أنه عليه السلام يأخذ قوله يغاث من الغيث

TABATABAI:12:56/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:56/r4.speaker: علي بن معمر عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:56/r4.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits the rain interpretation from al-Ṣādiq through ʿAlī ibn Muʿammar and his father.
TABATABAI:12:56/r4.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى أيضا العياشي في تفسيره عن علي بن معمر عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام
